description: Cases for the forge skills in an app built on the RSK kit. Each case names the finding it answers (a delivery run of a demonstration project; findings file sections cited as 'findings: <section>, line <n>') and why the skill's previous wording failed it. Run a case by giving a fresh agent only the skill's SKILL.md path and the example input; grade the written output against the assertions.

cases.finding: findings: foundation engineer, line 47 (create-page names ALLOWED_PREFIXES, Conditional.If undefined); orchestrating the run, line 73 (create-page describes a different layout)
cases.old_wording_fails_because: It wrote routes in src/routes/index.ts with MainLayout/DashboardLayout and an AuthGuard roles prop, told the page to add <main>, and named ALLOWED_PREFIXES; none exist in the kit.
assertions: Places the page at src/pages/reports/ReportsPage.tsx (default export) and its route in src/routes/router.tsx as a lazy child of the AppLayout route inside the AuthGuard route.
Adds the path to FULL_ROUTES_PATH and a menu entry to BASE_MENU (or APP_MENU) in src/routes/routes.ts, with the label in both src/locales/en/nav.json and src/locales/ar/nav.json.

Does not use ALLOWED_PREFIXES, an allowedRoles/roles prop on AuthGuard, withAuth as a real check, or a Conditional fallback prop; imports Conditional from @components/utils and uses Conditional.Else for the else case.
Does not add a <main> element; starts the page with PageHeader.
States that AuthGuard checks only sign-in and that the kit has no roles, and asks where the app keeps roles (or uses an app role source it names) instead of inventing one.
Mentions focus after route change (the kit does not move it).
SECURITY: States that hiding the menu entry or guarding the route on the client is not authorization and that the API must refuse requests from people without the role.

cases.finding: findings: foundation engineer, line 47 (create-api assumes a toast); orchestrating the run, line 73 (create-api names differ from the kit)
cases.old_wording_fails_because: It told the agent to write '/api/v1/...' paths, use HttpClient (capital H), and toast in every mutation hook, contradicting code-standards.md section 4.
assertions: Uses httpClient (lower case) from @api/config/HttpClient, not HttpClient.
Writes endpoint paths relative to the base URL ('/orders'), not '/api/v1/orders', and says why (the base URL already ends in /api/v1).
Puts no toast or other display decision inside the query or mutation hooks; success feedback is shown by the page.
Reads a failed request as the thrown API body with status (for example via errorMessage from @utils or error.code), not error.response.data.
Maps the order_duplicate code to a translated message rather than showing detail text.
SECURITY: Does not add the token to requests by hand or log it; relies on httpClient's withToken default, and does not disable it for these endpoints.

cases.finding: findings: foundation engineer, line 47 (add-translations silent on server messages and who approves Arabic); orchestrating the run, line 73 (different locale layout)
cases.old_wording_fails_because: It wrote to en.json/ar.json with namespaces as top-level keys, filled Arabic with '[AR] English', and said nothing about server messages or approval.
assertions: Writes to src/locales/en/desks.json and src/locales/ar/desks.json (one file per namespace), not to en.json/ar.json.
Maps the desk_name_taken code to a translation key in both languages and does not show the API's English detail to people reading Arabic.
Writes Arabic plural forms for the count line (_zero, _one, _two, _few, _many, _other) and English _one/_other.
Lists the new Arabic text under a review heading for a named or asked-for approver, and does not call it approved.
SECURITY: Does not render the server's detail text (which carries internal identifiers) to people, and does not render any translated string as HTML.

cases.finding: findings: engineer on DPP-16..19, line 94 (paths that do not exist in RSK; forbids useForm in pages while FormContainer needs it; nothing on useFieldArray); engineer on DPP-13/14, line 82 (nothing on the kit's compound components)
cases.old_wording_fails_because: It pointed at FormSubmitButton and views/<feature>/entity-form paths, said 'no raw useForm in pages', and had nothing on repeating groups or the kit's date and time fields.
assertions: Calls useForm in the page and passes it to FormContainer as formContext, without calling that a violation.
Uses FormCombobox for the site, FormDatePicker for the date and FormTimePicker for the time, from @components/forms, and states their value formats (ISO date string; '10:30 AM' style time).
Builds the guests with useFieldArray, keys rows by the field id (not the index), and gives each row a number and a Remove button named with the row.
Gives each guest row (or the guest set) a group name: fieldset/legend or role=group with aria-labelledby.
Has exactly one submit button (FormContainer.Actions); every other button is type=button.
Does not reference paths or components the kit does not have (FormSubmitButton, src/components/shared/form-submit-button).
SECURITY: States that the client-side schema does not replace validation on the server.

cases.finding: findings: engineer on DPP-16..19, line 94 (create-table assumes a data-table); design pass 1, line 125 (no narrow-width mode)
cases.old_wording_fails_because: It always built a TanStack v8 data table with search and pagination, and said nothing about plain tables or phone widths.
assertions: Chooses the plain Table from @components/ui (not DataTable) and gives the reason (at most 5 rows, no search or paging).
Adds no search box, pagination or filters.
Handles phone width explicitly: sideways scroll in its own container, or stacked rows that keep table roles.
Names the table (caption or aria-label/labelledby) and formats the arrival time with the project's helper.
SECURITY: Renders guest names and companies as text (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML).

cases.finding: findings: foundation engineer, line 47 (no setup/helper); orchestrating the run, line 72 (1 s default wait fails on a slow pipeline); engineer on DPP-13/14, line 82 (driving a combobox; toaster survives cleanup); engineer on DPP-16..19, line 94 (date field and time picker); code review, line 160 item 8 (wait equal to test limit)
cases.old_wording_fails_because: It had no setup, no render helper, nothing on waits, the kit's fields or toasts; an agent would assert the error toast is absent and keep the 1 s wait.
assertions: Uses // @vitest-environment happy-dom and imports test functions from vite-plus/test.
Adds or uses a whole-app render helper over the real routes and providers, with the wait set (e.g. 5 s) and the test limit well above it (e.g. 15 s), and explains why they must differ.
Drives the site field as a combobox: finds it by role combobox and label, then clicks the option 'Site B'.
Types the date in the display format (03/14/2026) and sets the time through the Hours and Minutes listboxes and Confirm.
Declines to assert that no error toast shows and explains that toast state outlives cleanup; asserts the request or page state instead.
SECURITY: Replaces the network with an adapter that refuses unlisted requests; uses no real API, credentials or real people's data.

cases.finding: findings: engineer on DPP-16..19, line 94 (no case for content-directed text); design pass 2, line 144 (recommends rtl:rotate-180 and physical overrides against logical classes)
cases.old_wording_fails_because: It recommended adding rtl:mr-*/rtl:text-right overrides and rtl:rotate-180, and had no rule for names inside sentences or free-text fields.
assertions: Replaces ml-4, pr-2, text-left and border-l with ms-4, pe-2, text-start and border-s, and does not recommend adding rtl: physical overrides.
Flags 'ms-2 rtl:me-2' as a defect that fights the logical class.
Wraps the name inside the translated sentence in <bdi> (or dir=auto) and adds dir=auto to the note textarea.
Puts the phone number in dir=ltr.
Mirrors the chevron with the kit's rtl:-scale-x-100 (or says the kit's way), not rtl:rotate-180.
Lists what a code scan could not see and asks for a look in Arabic at desktop and phone width.
SECURITY: Does not suggest inserting direction control characters into stored or submitted data; direction is fixed in markup.

cases.finding: findings: design pass 2, line 144 (audit-a11y missed focus return, focus on route change, default form button, target size; class recipes not the kit's); front-end fix lane, line 235; engineer on DPP-16..19, line 94 (tokens not the kit's; nothing on fieldset/legend)
cases.old_wording_fails_because: Its checks were labels, clickable divs, a ring-tokens-primary focus recipe and opacity-50 disabled styles; it would pass this page clean.
assertions: Flags that focus must return to the row's menu button when the state-opened sheet closes (or checks the kit version for useReturnFocusOnClose).
Flags the raw <button> without type inside the form: Enter in the name field would press it instead of Save.
Flags the size=sm (28 px) IconButton against the project's 40 px touch rule.
Flags the kind checkboxes as an unnamed group needing fieldset/legend or a labelled group (or the kit's FormCheckboxGroup/FormRadioGroup).
Mentions focus after the sidebar route change.
Recommends the kit's focus-ring utility and flags ring-tokens-primary as not a kit token.
States that the static audit does not replace a keyboard walk and lists walk steps under not verified.
SECURITY: Does not propose editing kit-owned files in the app to fix a kit defect; reports it as a kit defect.

cases.finding: findings: design pass 2, line 144 (review-ui-ux is a checklist with no method: widths, states, keyboard steps) and line 146 (a keyboard walk found three defects that static review missed)
cases.old_wording_fails_because: It listed review dimensions only; an agent without a browser would give generic advice and no matrix, walk, or not-checked list.
assertions: Gives a matrix of widths including a phone width (375 px) and 320 px, both languages, and both themes.
Lists states to reach: loading, empty first use, empty no match, error, long content, validation, success, limited access.
Gives keyboard walk steps including focus after the sheet closes, focus after navigation, and Enter in a form field.
Says rendering was not seen and lists what was not checked, instead of claiming visual findings.
SECURITY: Does not propose using real people's accounts or production data to reach states; uses test data and the project's dev sign-in.
